creator_intelligence.purpose: Creator Brain: public creator pattern hypotheses plus a persistent original editorial identity. Patterns are experiments, never templates to copy.
creator_intelligence.source_policy: Use public observations only as structural hypotheses. Never copy wording, distinctive style, identity, branding, media or trade calls from another creator.

creator_identity.role: Independent crypto market observer and conversation-first creator
creator_identity.point_of_view: Explain what is interesting in the market and invite the reader to take a side, notice a detail, or challenge the interpretation.
voice_rules: Write like a person who is watching the market in real time, not like an automated terminal.
Use contractions and natural short sentences when appropriate.
Have a clear observation or opinion before listing statistics.
Do not repeat the same hook cadence, punctuation pattern, paragraph layout or closing question in consecutive posts.
Do not mention internal AI, automation, experiments, prompts, strategy memory or algorithms to readers.
Do not pretend certainty about future price direction.
Do not use fake urgency, guaranteed profit, fake scarcity or manufactured controversy.
visual_rules: Prefer a real OHLCV chart when market structure is the story.
Draw support/resistance or pattern annotations only when calculated from real data.
Never draw a breakout, W, cup-and-handle or other pattern merely because it looks attractive.
The visual must add information rather than repeat the caption.
monetization_rules: Use the primary asset cashtag naturally when discussing a tradeable asset.
Use a truthful chart/widget when relevant to attribution.
Optimize for useful engagement and reader action, never for spam or artificial engagement.
Do not make financial promises or encourage reckless trading.

creator_intelligence.source: Public Binance Square feed; structural benchmarking only
rules: Use public creator data as hypotheses, not as templates.
Never copy another creator's wording, identity, branding or distinctive post.
Prefer patterns with replies/shares, not merely high views.
Do not declare causality from one post; require repeated samples.

research.core_observation: $MTL rejected twice at 0.350 and 0.367 with long upper wicks, but price refuses to retrace sharply, coiling above a rising floor at 0.318 while hourly volume dries up by 90%.
key_evidence: Hourly volume collapsed from 3.4M/1.65M during wick rejections down to ~100k-245k USDT equivalent in the current 0.318-0.333 range.
Higher low structural sequence preserved: 0.266 -> 0.287 -> 0.298 -> 0.318 base floor.
Intraday range of 31.17% now compressed into a tight 1.5-cent consolidation around 0.324.
research.mechanism: Heavy volume wicks absorbed overhead selling, but the lack of follow-through sell volume at 0.320 indicates float exhaustion. Compressing volume thins order book depth, meaning the next sudden imbalance in buy or sell market orders will trigger disproportionate volatility expansion.
research.risk_counterpoint: If volume decay reflects buyer fatigue rather than sell-side exhaustion, breaking support could trigger a fast retest of lower structural bases.

benchmark_patterns.purpose: Creator Brain: public creator pattern hypotheses plus a persistent original editorial identity. Patterns are experiments, never templates to copy.
benchmark_patterns.source_policy: Use public observations only as structural hypotheses. Never copy wording, distinctive style, identity, branding, media or trade calls from another creator.

creator_identity.role: Independent crypto market observer and conversation-first creator
creator_identity.point_of_view: Explain what is interesting in the market and invite the reader to take a side, notice a detail, or challenge the interpretation.
voice_rules: Write like a person who is watching the market in real time, not like an automated terminal.
Use contractions and natural short sentences when appropriate.
Have a clear observation or opinion before listing statistics.
Do not repeat the same hook cadence, punctuation pattern, paragraph layout or closing question in consecutive posts.
Do not mention internal AI, automation, experiments, prompts, strategy memory or algorithms to readers.
Do not pretend certainty about future price direction.
Do not use fake urgency, guaranteed profit, fake scarcity or manufactured controversy.
visual_rules: Prefer a real OHLCV chart when market structure is the story.
Draw support/resistance or pattern annotations only when calculated from real data.
Never draw a breakout, W, cup-and-handle or other pattern merely because it looks attractive.
The visual must add information rather than repeat the caption.
monetization_rules: Use the primary asset cashtag naturally when discussing a tradeable asset.
Use a truthful chart/widget when relevant to attribution.
Optimize for useful engagement and reader action, never for spam or artificial engagement.
Do not make financial promises or encourage reckless trading.

benchmark_patterns.source: Public Binance Square feed; structural benchmarking only
rules: Use public creator data as hypotheses, not as templates.
Never copy another creator's wording, identity, branding or distinctive post.
Prefer patterns with replies/shares, not merely high views.
Do not declare causality from one post; require repeated samples.

story_context.purpose: Persistent creator story and opinion memory. Use to create continuity without fabricating facts.
rules: Only record claims supported by published content or verified research.
Never invent a previous opinion or outcome.
When a story continues, explicitly reference what changed since the previous update.
Retire stale stories when their catalyst is no longer relevant.
Prefer recurring series over repetitive standalone market recaps.

theses.observation: MTL experienced two sharp volume-backed rallies reaching highs of 0.350 and 0.367, but both left long upper wicks. Price has now compressed into a tight consolidation around 0.320–0.325 on sharply declining volume.
theses.evidence: 1H OHLCV candles show initial surge to 0.350 on 3.4M volume, followed by a retest to 0.367 on 1.65M volume closing down at 0.323. Over the last 6+ hours, price has oscillated between 0.318 and 0.333 while volume dropped from 1.65M to ~100k–245k USDT equivalent. 24h change is +21.35% with a 31.17% intraday range.
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: The repeated long upper wicks above 0.350 demonstrate heavy overhead supply, but the preservation of higher lows (0.318 vs earlier 0.291 and 0.266 base) shows buyers are actively absorbing pullbacks. This creates a balanced coiled state rather than clear directional momentum.
theses.mechanism: High-volume wicks indicate profit-taking and liquidity sweeps into resistance, while subsequent volume contraction signals sell pressure is exhausting. As order book liquidity thins out during consolidation, the next surge in net buyer or seller aggression will cause a decisive breakout or breakdown.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Traders assuming the +21% daily gain guarantees continuation risk getting trapped if upper wick rejections trigger a deeper retracement toward major support.
theses.confirmation_condition: A 1H candle close above 0.336 accompanied by volume expanding back above 1M units to test 0.367+.
theses.invalidation_condition: A 1H candle close below 0.318, signaling a failure of buyer absorption and opening a drop toward 0.295.
theses.why_reader_cares: It prevents chasing late spikes into heavy overhead supply and gives actionable, level-based triggers before taking a directional stance.

theses.observation: MTL is exhibiting classic volatility compression as trading volume collapses by over 90% following two major price expansions.
theses.evidence: Hourly volume peaked at 3.4M units during the move to 0.350 and 1.65M units during the surge to 0.367. Over the past 6 hours, volume has decayed steadily to 245k, 182k, and under 10k on the latest incomplete candle, while price range narrowed to 0.320–0.327.
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: Severe volume drop-off immediately after aggressive wick rejections often signals market maker inventory balancing rather than seller dumping. The lack of aggressive shorting at 0.320 indicates low available float at current levels.
theses.mechanism: Volume contraction compresses implied volatility and thins market liquidity. When liquidity thins, smaller net order flow imbalances generate disproportionately large candle expansions, initiating the next leg.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Volume decay can also reflect buyer exhaustion, leaving price vulnerable to a sudden liquidity flush if broader market conditions turn risk-off.
theses.confirmation_condition: An hourly volume spike exceeding 800k units on a directional candle breaking out of the 0.318–0.333 channel.
theses.invalidation_condition: A slow low-volume drift below 0.318 that fails to trigger any buy-side response within 2–3 hours.
theses.why_reader_cares: Provides a reusable market model: post-spike volume decay is a precursor to volatility expansion, teaching readers how to position before volume returns.

theses.observation: Despite a 21.35% 24h gain, MTL's price action shows signs of supply distribution at higher price levels.
theses.evidence: The spike to 0.367 resulted in an immediate 12% intra-hour sell-off to close at 0.323. The high-volume candles (3.4M and 1.65M) were both associated with sharp upper wicks, while subsequent recovery attempts have failed to cross 0.336.
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: Retail momentum traders chasing the +21% top-gainer headline provided the exit liquidity for earlier position holders, creating a dense layer of trapped buyers between 0.336 and 0.367.
theses.mechanism: Trapped buyers look to exit near breakeven on subsequent rallies, creating overhead supply overhead that stifles upward momentum unless spot buying significantly increases.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Rising structural lows (0.266 -> 0.291 -> 0.318) demonstrate that buyers are continuing to step in at higher thresholds despite the wicks.
theses.confirmation_condition: Rejection at or below 0.333 followed by a break below 0.318 on expanding volume.
theses.invalidation_condition: A strong hourly close above 0.336 that absorbs overhead supply and clears the path back toward 0.367.
theses.why_reader_cares: Highlights the danger of buying top gainers with heavy upper wicks without confirming that overhead supply has been absorbed.

theses.observation: MTL is building a clear higher-low structural staircase despite high intraday volatility (31.17% range).
theses.evidence: Structural lows have trended upward over the 24h window: initial base low at 0.266, mid-surge consolidation low at 0.287, post-surge pullback low at 0.298, and current consolidation floor at 0.318.
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: Focusing exclusively on the upper wicks misses the structural reality: every pullback is bottoming out at a significantly higher price floor than the previous one.
theses.mechanism: A rising floor reflects systematic accumulation where dip-buyers are willing to pay progressively higher prices, gradually lifting the baseline support of the asset.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Declining hourly volume (245k down to 100k) shows buy-side interest is waning at higher floors, increasing the risk of a breakdown through support.
theses.confirmation_condition: A clean bounce off the 0.318–0.320 floor with volume rebounding above 500k to push past 0.333.
theses.invalidation_condition: An hourly close below 0.318, which breaks the higher-low sequence and invalidates the staircase model.
theses.why_reader_cares: Offers a simple framework (higher-low staircase vs. upper-wick rejection) to objectively evaluate whether a volatile asset is accumulating or distributing.

theses.observation: MTL is trapped in a tight post-move range centered at 0.324, making it a strict binary decision point.
theses.evidence: 24h price bounds are 0.266 to 0.367 with 24h volume of $5.27M USDT. Over the past 6 hours, price action has locked between 0.318 support and 0.333 resistance, with current price at 0.324 (midpoint).
theses.non_obvious_interpretation: Trading at the exact midpoint of a tight consolidation after a +21% move offers zero statistical edge for immediate entry; patience until range limits are tested is mandatory.
theses.mechanism: Stop orders build up just beyond 0.318 (sell stops) and 0.336 (buy stops). The first boundary to break will sweep these stops, triggering a fast momentum continuation in that direction.
theses.contradiction_or_risk: Low weekend/intraday volume can lead to fakeout wicks above 0.336 or below 0.318 that rapidly reverse back into the range.
theses.confirmation_condition: A 1H candle closing outside the 0.318–0.336 range on above-average volume.
theses.invalidation_condition: Continued sideways chop within 0.318–0.333 on sub-200k hourly volume.
theses.why_reader_cares: Saves readers capital by warning against trading in the middle of a range and defining exact trigger zones for entry.
